title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
Linking to GEOS 3.13.0, GDAL 3.8.5, PROJ 9.5.1; sf_use_s2() is TRUE
The aim of this note is to examine the different statistical and cartographical sources of interest for the objectives of the REDEC project.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
The map of INSEE
The geometry of voting offices has been made available only very recently by INSEE through an automatic recognition of the location of adresses on listings (INSEE, 2023, Proposition de contour des bureaux de vote). The raw map offers a complete coverage of the territory of the departement :









The geometry of map is relatively simple in rural areas where voting offices correspond to the geometry of a commune or an aggregate of communes. But situation is more complex in urban areas.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
Generalisation of the map
We have created a simplified map using Voronoï triangulation applied to the geometric center of the area covered by voting offices. As a consequence, some details are lost but the map become more easy to use for topological and spatial analysis.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
Cartogram transformation
As we are interested in election, we realize a third version of the map of voting officies where the area is made proportional to the number of registred people (inscrits). We use the presidential election of 2022 as reference.

title: Geomatic database of REDEC project
text:
Filosofi 2021
The INSEE grid of population Filosofi at the resolution of 200m x 200m has been published in 2021 with a set of 30 indicators describing the population by age and sex and some economic and social indicator derived from census like the median income of the houshold, the share of social housing, etc. This resolution of 200m is generally sufficient to charactrize the situation of voting office, even if some approximation is requested in central urban area. As an example, here is the distribution of voting office and grid data inthe capital city of the département.

title: Visualisation tool
text:
We propose to visualize the delineation of circonscription with two complementary maps.


We use here the classical map in geometric space with eucldean distance. We can therefore viusalize large surfaces corresponding to low density area and small surfaces corresponding to high density area.












We use here a cartogramme transformation of voting office in order to produce a demographic space where the area is proportional to the number of people officially allowed to vote. The distance between two points is the number of inhabitant between origin and destination (the Stouffer distance).

Objective
The aim of this note is to experiment methods of classification with population and euclidean distance constraint. They don not fulfill necessarily the contiguity constraint but offers some interesting results for discussion

section: 3. k-means applied to voting office with demographic distance
text:
3. k-means applied to voting office with demographic distance
Suppose now that we use as initial building blocks the division in 804 voting offices, withour considering the limits of communes as a constraint. In the case of Val-de-Marne, the size of voting office is very regular because each commune has a sufficient population to have several voting office.And we can suppose that their maximum size is defined by the law.


`stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.









We use it a map where the geometry has been transformed in order tomake the area proportional to the number of registred people (inscrits). It is therefoer a demographic space whee the distance between two point is not a number of kilometers but a number of people. What is called by the sociologist Samuel Stouffer (1942) an amount of intervening opportunities.









The coordinates in this demographic space to benefit from some interesting properties and make possible to use existing algorithm of classification. We can for example use classification methods based on distance like k-means without constraint and examine the results of clustering for 11 circonscriptions

title: K-means clustering in demographic space
section: 4. K-means in demographic space with equal size constraint
text:
4. K-means in demographic space with equal size constraint
Some authors has developped methods that take into account a constraint of equal size of cluster. As an example we have use the function balanced_cluster() of the package anticluster which make possible to obtain cluster with exacly the same number of individuals. Unfortunately the authors of the package has decided that “exactly means exactly” … which means that we are obliged to “cheat” our data if the number of units can not be divided by the number of expected cluster … In our example, we have 804 units to be divided in 11 circonscription and the program does not work as it can not be divided by 11 without decimal. But if we aggregate only two offices with their neighbors, we arrive at 803 units which can be divided by 11 \(803/11 ==73\)
The algorithm will produce circonscriptions with the same number of voting office. And as the voting office has generally equivalent size, the result will be approximatively equivalent when we aggregate.

title: K-means clustering in demographic space
text:
Discussion
This analysis confirms that the legal obligation to build circonscription has aggregates of communes limits the possibility to reach optimal solutions and create a legal confusion between two elections. The cantons are instrument of local elections (département) when circonscription are instrument of national elections. Using the voting office as building blocks would be more logical if we admit that a member of the parliament is not defending a local area but elabrating national policy …

title: REDEC
text: This github directory is used for cartographic experiments in relation with the submission of the REDEC project to the AAPG 2026 of the ANR. We will more precisely focus onthe analysis of four cases studies related to the département of Isère, Maine-et-Loire, Somme and Val-de-Marne.

title: REDEC
text:
Selection of cases studies
Four département has been carefully chosen as places of experiment of the different methods and concepts developed in previous work packages. These four case studies will be used ex-ante in order to test methods and concepts that will be further applied to the whole territory of France. They will also be used ex-post as proof of concept for researcher and decision maker. And finally they will be used as test for the research of the best way to disseminate the results toward stakeholders and citizens. To achieve this objectives, the four cases studies has been chosen in order to represent both geographical complexity and political diversity of situations :
– Val-de-Marne (94) is a metropolitan département located in the suburb of Paris with a very high population density concentrated in very few communes which implies necessarily to break some of them in order to have equal population size in cantons. The political opinion is characterized by equivalent proportion of votes for left and center-right but very few votes for far-right.
– Isère (38) offers the case of a département which combines very strong geographical and political differences. The density of population is very high in the metropolitan agglomeration of Grenoble and the related valleys but very low in mountains area. The political diversity is complete with far-right in the north, far-left in the suburb of Grenoble and center-left or center right elsewhere.
– Somme (80) is a good example of rural and industrial area that has been exposed to economic crisis and has recently offers a majority of vote to far-right, with the exception of the capital city of Amiens. Furthermore, the strange shape of some of its districts raises questions. It is also a remarkable case of gerrymandering with three strange circonscriptions having the form of an octopus (n°4) and a salamander (n°1) surrounding a frog (n°2) …
– Maine-et-Loire (49) located in the Western part of France is the opposite example of Somme in political terms as it remains a typical area or resistance of center-right or center-left.It is also characterized by an interesting administrative evolution with a strong reduction of the number of communes by merging (Bideau 2024). We arrive at a moment where some cluster of rural communes are larger than cantons.

title: REDEC
text:
Data collection
We will firstly examine which data can be collected and combine at different levels in each of the selected area.

title: REDEC
text:
Experiments
We will then realize preliminary experiments of redisctricting applied to the electoral circonscription. The objective will be to compare the current offcial division against alternative proposals.
